naming_clarity.reason: Plain stakeholder vocabulary (vehicle safety engineer, high-voltage circuit, safe voltage window, workshop, fault entry, service reset); thermal runaway and service reset are standard domain terms a safety engineer or workshop can confirm, and the guidance asks for leniency on domain terminology.

no_mechanism_leak.reason: Describes behaviour only (leaving the high-voltage circuit, a stored fault entry, a service reset) and names no class, function, module, table, endpoint or technology; it does not even name the contactors, the memory or the diagnostic protocol.

parent_fit.reason: Root of the V: the user_stories stage has no upstream stage (depends_on is empty) and the story has no outgoing trace link, so there is no parent to engage with and the axis is fully met by default.

single_user_capability.reason: Centred on one capability, the pack removing itself from the high-voltage circuit when a cell or current limit is violated and staying out until a service reset, but it also folds in a workshop diagnostic aspect (a stored fault entry naming the cell or sensor and the limit) that has a different observer and could arguably ship separately.
single_user_capability.suggestion: Keep this story on the protective disconnect with its hold until a service reset, and move the stored fault entry for the workshop into its own diagnostics story (or state why the record cannot ship without the disconnect).

user_observable.reason: Every observable names an observer and a visible effect: the vehicle loses drive power as the pack disconnects, the workshop reads a stored fault entry naming the cell or sensor and the limit, a bench forcing a cell past a limit sees the disconnect command within a bounded time, and the pack stays open until a service reset.

summary: Clear, observable, implementation-free protective-disconnect story, but it folds in a workshop-facing stored fault entry that could arguably ship separately.
